questions.question: Which of the following is the local name of Dussehra festival celebrated in the state of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The Kullu Dussehra is the world-famous local name for the Dussehra festival celebrated in the state of Himachal Pradesh.
  • Unique Timing: Unlike the rest of India, it begins on the day when the ten-day Dussehra festival ends elsewhere.
  • Deity: It centers around the worship of Lord Raghunath and is held at the Dhalpur Maidan in Kullu.
  • International Status: It was declared an international festival in 1972 and attracts tourists for its vibrant chariot procession.

questions.question: Konark festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Konark Festival is a major cultural event celebrated in the state of Odisha.
  • Venue: It is held against the backdrop of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Sun Temple in Konark.
  • Nature: It is primarily a classical dance festival where maestros of Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Manipuri, and Kathak perform.
Note: It is usually held in December every year alongside the International Sand Art Festival.

questions.question: The ________ festival, in which the serpent goddess Mansa is worshipped, is celebrated in some parts of Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand in India.
questions.solution:
The Bihula festival is celebrated in parts of Bihar, Bengal, and Jharkhand, where the serpent goddess Mansa is worshipped.
  • Legend: The festival is associated with the story of Bihula and Lakshindar, highlighting the devotion of a wife to save her husband from a snake bite.
  • Mansa Puja: Goddess Mansa is considered the daughter of Lord Shiva and the protector of humans from snake-related calamities.

questions.question: Shigmo festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Shigmo festival (or Shishirotsava) is a vibrant spring festival celebrated in the state of Goa.
  • Community: It is predominantly celebrated by the Konkani Hindu community.
  • Activities: It features traditional folk dances like Ghode Modni and Fugdi, colorful street parades, and enactments of mythological scenes.
  • Significance: It is the Goan counterpart of Holi and marks the farewell of winter.

questions.question: Which festival of Nagaland usually begins on 1 December, every year?
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival is the most famous festival of Nagaland, which traditionally begins on 1st December (Nagaland Statehood Day).
  • Nature: Known as the 'Festival of Festivals', it brings together all the tribes of Nagaland to showcase their traditional arts, dances, and food.
  • Venue: Most of the events take place at the Naga Heritage Village in Kisama.

questions.question: Which national festival of India falls on the 26th of January?
questions.solution:
Republic Day is the national festival of India celebrated on 26th January every year.
  • Significance: It commemorates the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950, replacing the Government of India Act (1935).
  • Highlight: The main celebration is held at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath) in New Delhi, featuring a grand military and cultural parade.

questions.question: हाल्दा महोत्सव किस राज्य में मनाया जाता है?
questions.solution:
हाल्दा महोत्सव (Halda Festival) मुख्य रूप से हिमाचल प्रदेश के लाहौल घाटी में मनाया जाता है।
  • अवधि: यह त्योहार माघ पूर्णिमा के आसपास मनाया जाता है और दो दिनों तक चलता है।
  • महत्व: यह नए साल के आगमन का प्रतीक है और इसमें रोशनी के लिए देवदार की लकड़ियों की मशालें जलाई जाती हैं।
  • देवता: यह धन की देवी 'शशिकर आपा' (Shashikar Apa) को समर्पित है।

questions.question: Which of the following is mainly observed by the Christian community?
questions.solution:
Good Friday is a day observed primarily by the Christian community to commemorate the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his death at Calvary.
  • Nature: It is a day of solemnity, fasting, and prayer rather than celebration.
  • Easter: It falls on the Friday before Easter Sunday, which marks the resurrection of Jesus.

questions.question: Dhanu Yatra celebration of Odisha, which is also the largest open-air theatre in the world, is based on _________.
questions.solution:
The Dhanu Yatra of Bargarh, Odisha, is widely considered the world's largest open-air theatre.
  • Theme: It is based on Krishna Leela, specifically the story of Lord Krishna's visit to Mathura and the death of the tyrant King Kansa.
  • Scale: During the festival, the entire town of Bargarh transforms into Mathura, and the nearby Ambapali area becomes Gopapura.

questions.question: In which of the following places are Reh and Boori Boot predominantly celebrated?
questions.solution:
The festivals of Reh and Boori Boot are predominantly celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Reh: It is the most important festival of the Idu Mishmi tribe, celebrated for peace and prosperity.
  • Boori Boot: It is celebrated by the Nyishi tribe to welcome spring and pray for a successful harvest.

questions.question: The New Year as per the Assamese calendar coincides with the beginning of the harvest season, which is also known as ______ Bihu.
questions.solution:
The Assamese New Year coincides with the Bohag Bihu (also known as Rongali Bihu), which marks the beginning of the harvest season.
  • Timing: It is celebrated in mid-April and marks the start of the Assamese calendar.
  • Types of Bihu: Maagh Bihu is the harvest festival in January, and Kaati Bihu is a somber festival in October related to the growth of crops.
